scope: Actual supplied two-layer DXFs, not regenerated geometry. Prescribed permanent-magnet free-space force at imposed balanced currents. Not measured performance, manufacturing acceptance or a new power calculation.

files.changes: Swap B/C consistently in string groups, including layer definitions, LINE/VERTEX/POLYLINE references and via layers. Numeric groups and every other byte remain unchanged. Reverse swap reproduces original bytes exactly.

topology.interpretation: Each phase is continuous but is a resistor mesh, not one unbranched wire. Crossing vias join the parallel braid paths. Physical Z, not L1/L5/L6 name suffixes, sets copper planes.

assumptions.current_law: I_j = sin(2*pi*x/12mm + reference - j*120deg), j=0,1,2 for A,B,C; currents sum to zero
assumptions.trace_width_caveat: LINE entities contain centerlines, not physical trace widths. Uniform 0.2mm is declared, not inferred from unrelated defaults or DXF TRACEWID. Width sensitivity 0.127/0.2/0.35mm changes branch fractions by less than 1.6e-11A/A for these networks.

hypothetical_compact_C_terminal_reversal.scope: Force-sign diagnostic only. Requires physical winding-end reconnection, NOT negating one inverter phase command. No compact replacement routing was built or validated.

conclusions: The compact file as connected conflicts with conventional balanced ABC drive because C winding polarity is reversed relative to the spread file, even after the requested B/C relabeling.
This is not severe cancellation inside either supplied two-layer phase. Their individual phase force amplitudes are almost unchanged.

Opening displacement changes C circulation. Spreading is one way to get the required polarity, not an electromagnetic spacing requirement. A compact series-aiding reconnection remains possible in principle but is not implemented here.
Simply swapping B/C labels, or moving the controller's common electrical zero, does not reverse one winding's terminal polarity.
The four-layer cancellation receipts do not describe these two-layer DXFs.
